objective: Computation and proof. Where a removal opens two or more cuts of a chain or tree, classify the kept knots by the opened cuts they cross. Ask which are generated by eliminations from knots crossing no opened cut, which need knots crossing one, and which are new. Record also how an opened hub composes: through the tied pair or the released port, or only through the interface jointly.
status: Proved by SPLICE-TREE-20261102-001C-P001 (finite classification): opened cuts interact, and no hub-level feature decides how. The touching-hub hypothesis fails both ways; on 96 chains of K4^(3) and Fano pieces carried and joint knots occur with disjoint and touching hubs, at and away from shared ports, through and off the removed line's hub; every joint knot has 3 or 4 points; K4^(3)-only chains create nothing; derivations never grow, so bounded closures are exact; HUB-GLUE C's count reproduced up to tie classes
title: Do opened cuts interact?
